That locator distinguishes the passage from loose internet attributions: readers can return to the named work or section to check translation, surrounding argument, and edition-specific wording.

About Léopold Sédar Senghor

Léopold Sédar Senghor (1906–2001) was a Senegalese poet, theorist of Négritude, and Senegal’s first president. With Césaire and Damas he forged a black cultural affirmation in French; his essays treat Négritude as an ontology and aesthetics of vital force as well as a politics of cultural rendezvous.

How to read this passage

Social philosophy asks how individuals and collectives constitute each other, and what justice requires of shared life. This passage enters that discussion through society, dialogue, humanity.

Concepts in this quote

Society
Society is the web of institutions, customs, and mutual expectations in which individual freedom takes shape.
Dialogue
Dialogue appears in this archive as a live philosophical concern—not a slogan. These verified English passages show how thinkers treat dialogue as a problem of judgment, practice, or explanation.
Humanity
Humanity names both the species and the moral quality of being humane—bridging anthropology and ethics.
